subject: Stability coverage & SLA fallback playbook for Hosted API (p50 / p95 measurement)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
To: Opsly Sales <sales@opsly.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stability coverage & SLA fallback playbook for Hosted API (p50 / p95 measurement)

Hi Maya / Opsly team,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our commitment to make SLAs operationally clear, attached is a draft SLA tailored for your Hosted deployment, plus a short "measurement playbook" that explains how we compute p50/p95 and how we handle transient bursts. High-level summary below and a few questions where we need Opsly input.

Summary (what Redwood proposes):
- Committed latencies: p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 220ms (measured at the API ingress for successful text-generation requests, excluding cold-starts).
- Measurement approach: rolling 24-hour epoch to calculate contractual p50/p95; short-term sliding windows (10m p50, 30m p95) for operational alerts.
- Grace / carveouts: automated burst carveout when moving-average request rate exceeds baseline by >6x for >5 minutes; maintenance carveouts for pre-notified windows; transient routing fallback carveouts when downstream region is unreachable.
- Remediation: service credits calculated as percent of monthly invoice scaled by breach magnitude and duration.

Questions for Opsly:
1) Do you prefer the p95 measurement to include cross-region routing fallback latency or treat fallback as a separate failure mode?
2) What is your contract month boundary? (We default to calendar month but can align to your billing cycle.)

Next steps: please review the attached SLA/Playbook. If the high-level is acceptable, we can lock the commitment and send a DocuSign packet. I can also set up a 30-minute technical alignment call with Ben and our SREs to walk the measurement details.

- Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the draft — looks helpful. Quick clarifying points from our side:
- For us, p95 should reflect user-facing latency as much as possible. If a routing fallback causes an additional hop but the request still succeeds within reasonable time, we want that reflected in the p95; however, we also want a carveout path if the fallback is effectively a full region outage.
- We bill on the 1st of the month (calendar month).
- Can you confirm whether cached responses (prefix cache) are included in the measurement? Some of our internal load is highly cached and we'd like that to count toward the p50 (it improves the user experience).

We'd like to schedule the technical call — is tomorrow at 10am ET possible?

Thanks,
Maya Gonzalez

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stability coverage & SLA fallback playbook for Hosted API (p50 / p95 measurement)

Aditya —

Looping in Naomi for legal nuance and Ben for SRE detail. My proposed position for the Opsly ask:

1) Include cached responses in the contractual p50/p95 (we measure at ingress after any cache hit accounting). It reflects actual user experience and avoids perverse incentives not to cache. We should explicitly call out cache-hit annotation in the metric so Opsly can break down results.

2) Routing fallbacks: treat as part of p50/p95 unless the fallback triggers an automated region failover AND the failover crosses our documented outage threshold (we can define that as region loss for >3 minutes with >10% of requests affected). In that case we record a regional outage and exclude that epoch from contractual calculation, while still providing credits.

3) Measurement windows: maintain a rolling 24-hour contractual epoch. For operational visibility, publish 10-minute p50 and 30-minute p95 rolling windows as alerts. This two-tier approach reduces noise for billing while giving Opsly immediate notice of degradations.

4) Burst carveout: recommend a simple moving-average threshold (6x baseline sustained for >5 minutes) and require Opsly to provide any exogenous traffic-intent evidence (marketing campaigns, bulk re-ingestion) for retrospective carveout approval.

I attached a short "measurement playbook" that Ben and I drafted describing the exact computation steps and the fields we'll publish in the console (percentiles, sample counts, cache-hit flag, routing-tag). Ben — can you confirm the compute/collection practicality and whether synthetic probe baselines are feasible?

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stability coverage & SLA fallback playbook for Hosted API (p50 / p95 measurement)

TL;DR: All proposed items are implementable with small caveats — here's the safe, auditable approach we should offer Opsly.

Implementation notes: 
- Where we measure: at API ingress after any prefix/kv cache resolution. We stamp token-level attributes: cache_hit=true/false, route_fallback=true/false, region_id, and request_size_tokens. The contractual p50/p95 will be computed from the ingress timestamps for requests with 2xx responses.
- Cold starts / model warmup: exclude first request for an instance within 45s of spin-up. We'll surface counts for transparency.
- Routing fallbacks: include in the p50/p95 by default. Define a separate "regional outage" record when: route_fallback=true for >10% requests and the condition persists for >3 minutes. When a regional outage is recorded we will exclude that time window from contractual billing calculation and apply the outage remediation terms.
- Caching: include cached responses; we'll publish cache-hit broken down p50/p95 so Opsly can see the split.
- Synthetic probes: we can run a small fleet of probes per region (configurable) that exercise the same model/route and provide a baseline. These are separate telemetry and not included in contractual numbers but valuable for debugging.

Open question for legal: how granular should the sample-count floor be before we treat a p95 as "insufficient data"? I suggest a 30-sample floor per 24-hour epoch for a given route. Naomi — your thoughts?

Attachments: measurement-spec.yaml (brief schema for the telemetry we will publish).

—Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Finalized measurement approach & next steps — Hosted API SLA (Opsly)

Hi Maya / Opsly team,

Thanks for the quick turn. Based on the thread and internal alignment, here's the finalized approach we propose (we've updated the attached SLA draft accordingly).

Final summary: 
- Contract metrics: p50 and p95 measured at ingress for successful responses (2xx), including cached responses. Cold-start exclusion: first request post-instance spin-up within 45s.
- Contract epoch: rolling 24-hour window evaluated at end-of-day UTC for contractual accounting; operational alerts via 10-minute p50 and 30-minute p95 sliding windows.
- Regional outage carveout: detect and record a regional outage when route_fallback=true affects >10% of requests for a contiguous >3 minute interval; that contiguous epoch will be excluded from contractual calculation and handled under outage remediation terms.
- Burst carveout: automated when moving-average rate >6x baseline for >5 minutes; retrospective carveout requires Opsly-provided evidence for traffic spike (e.g., marketing campaign IDs).
- Remediation: credits scale with breach magnitude and duration; formula in section 4 of the attached SLA.

Next steps: 
1) If this aligns with Opsly, we'll upload the DocuSign packet (link below) for signature.
2) Book a 30-minute technical alignment (Ben + SREs) to walk the measurement fields and dashboard. Proposed time: Fri, Oct 16, 10:00am ET.

Best,
Aditya
